title: thymus serpyllum f. kosteleckyanus
intro: Thymus serpyllum f. kosteleckyanus, commonly known as creeping thyme, is a subspecies of the thyme plant, characterized by its low-growing, spreading habit and fragrant foliage. This herb is valued for its health benefits, which include its antimicrobial and antifungal properties, making it effective against respiratory infections, wounds, and skin conditions. The therapeutic actions of creeping thyme include its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and exhibit antioxidant properties, which contribute to its use in aromatherapy and herbal medicine. The bioactive constituents of creeping thyme include thymol, carvacrol, and ursolic acid, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and contribute to its use in traditional medicine.
